entries.title: Beslan school massacre triggers a dispute over language in headlines
entries.report: A columnist condemned perceived journalistic euphemisms for the gunmen in the **Beslan, Russia school siege**, stating that **some 400 people** had died and comparing words used by international newsrooms.
entries.assess: **A polemic about terminology and an approximate early casualty figure, not a final victim register or impartial media study.** The European Court's later case summary describes **approximately 334 civilian deaths, including 186 children**; detailed responsibility and the state's response remained subjects of legal review.

leadingCandidate.evidence: report; curated candidate; headline and report reviewed

entries.title: First Indian Ocean tsunami reports give a toll above 50,000
entries.report: A reflection on the recent **December 26** Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami said **more than 50,000** had died and warned that contaminated water could complicate relief.
entries.assess: **An extremely early partial toll, not the full catastrophe.** NOAA's later global historical dataset attributes approximately **227,899 deaths** to the earthquake and tsunami, a differently dated and much more complete estimate. The source is evidence of how incomplete the picture still was that week.

entries.title: High-school coverage revises tsunami magnitude of human loss
entries.report: A student feature on rebuilding after the Indian Ocean tsunami reported **more than 220,000 deaths** and described relief and reconstruction across several countries.
entries.assess: **An updated early-2005 estimate, sharply higher than the preceding December's >50,000 count, and close to NOAA's later roughly 227,899.** The figure and geographic reach differ because the news was no longer a first-week snapshot; pledges of aid are not proof that funds were disbursed.

entries.title: Rabbi recounts relative's survival of London transit attacks
entries.report: Rabbi **Shea Hecht** wrote of trouble reaching family by telephone after the **July 7** bombings and retold his brother-in-law **Rabbi Aryeh Sufrin's** experience on a London Underground train affected by the attacks.
entries.assess: **A secondhand family-survivor narrative, not a list of all four attackers, trains, or victims.** British official records establish **52 victims killed**, excluding the bombers; the religious interpretation of survival is the writer's own.

entries.title: Katrina front page shows evacuees in immediate need of basics
entries.report: With the headline **“Hell and High Water,”** the *Recorder* pictured **Cabrini Cooper** holding her infant daughter at a shelter in Florida, reporting that hundreds of New Orleans evacuees were receiving their first clean clothes, meals, and showers in days.
entries.assess: **A photographic and named human story, not a regional survey of survivors' conditions.** The tragedy followed Katrina's August **29** Gulf Coast landfall and catastrophic flooding; later official casualty and infrastructure investigations are separate from this immediate relief scene.

entries.title: Delayed Katrina response becomes the subject of political anger
entries.report: A writer denounced what was presented as days of delay by federal agencies in sending troops and supplies to **New Orleans**, comparing the response with national urgency after September 11. The page suggested conditions improved swiftly after military arrivals.
entries.assess: **A forceful contemporary account and political judgment, not a verified hour-by-hour response log.** Later government reviews documented multiple failures and strengths in preparedness and response; the article's timing and 'order restored' statements need operational corroboration.

entries.title: Former Muncie resident recounts Katrina evacuation
entries.report: Former Muncie resident **Runako Tsitsi Kumbula** described her experience in New Orleans as Hurricane Katrina approached, including the frightening effort to leave and later confrontation with the storm's damage.
entries.assess: **A survivor's own perspective rather than a statistical sample of evacuees.** It deserves preservation in her voice without extrapolating one route or outcome to the entire displaced population.

entries.title: Katrina's damage still listed as $63 billion with higher projections
entries.report: A hurricane-cost graphic placed **Katrina at $63 billion**, with a parenthetical warning that estimates could climb to **$200 billion**, while discussing other Gulf storms including **Rita**. The graphic mixed historical storms and monetary values.
entries.assess: **Provisional storm-loss projections, not comparable settled figures.** Realized insured loss, overall economic harm, inflation-adjusted cost, and different geographic/time boundaries must be distinguished before ranking hurricanes; the unusually wide 2005 range illustrates ongoing uncertainty.

entries.title: Muncie holds a resource fair for relocated Katrina families
entries.report: The paper reported a **Horizon Convention Center** resource fair organized with United Way to help **at least 54 displaced families known to be living in Muncie** find work, housing, and support.
entries.assess: **A local service-provider count at one date, not a census of all Gulf Coast evacuees or all families in Indiana.** It documents a concrete secondary migration and civic response weeks after the storm.

entries.title: Pakistan earthquake article shows a rapidly rising death toll
entries.report: Student writer **Amy Greer** described the **October 8** Kashmir earthquake, reporting an earlier estimate near **20,000 deaths** had already risen to about **35,000** as buildings collapsed and survivors were rescued.
entries.assess: **Interim fatality counts, not a certified final register.** USGS identifies the main earthquake as magnitude **7.6**; exact totals differ across official reporting agencies and geographic definitions, so a final number should not be inferred from this article.

entries.title: Indianapolis bird-flu preparedness becomes front-page news
entries.report: A local feature asked whether Indianapolis could respond if **H5N1 avian influenza** began spreading widely among people, with many citizens doubting institutional preparedness after Katrina.
entries.assess: **A plausible preparedness question, not evidence that an H5N1 human pandemic was occurring in Indiana.** The CDC reported **no identified human H5N1 cases in the United States** in its late-2005 assessment and no demonstrated sustained person-to-person transmission.

entries.title: Rosa Parks's death prompts reflection on the choice to resist
entries.report: A remembrance considered the consequences had **Rosa Parks** complied with Montgomery bus segregation in **1955**, treating her refusal and her life of civil-rights activism as a legacy of moral courage.
entries.assess: **A counterfactual tribute, not proof that the movement depended on only one person or moment.** Parks died **October 24, 2005**; the Library of Congress holds records documenting her earlier activism, community organizing, and subsequent work beyond the famous bus protest.

leadingCandidate.evidence: report; curated candidate; headline and report reviewed

entries.title: President outlines pandemic vaccine stockpile proposal
entries.report: A dispatch said **President George W. Bush** requested funding to prepare a vaccine supply for **20 million Americans** against the then-current bird-flu threat and called for stronger vaccine-production protections.
entries.assess: **A proposal and projection about possible future pandemic risk, not evidence that the specified vaccine doses had already been manufactured or that a human H5N1 pandemic had begun.** Separate authorization, procurement, and epidemiology records would be needed to judge implementation.

entries.title: Charitable appeals compete after tsunami, hurricanes, and Pakistan quake
entries.report: The newspaper quoted a philanthropy survey reporting, by **December 15**, approximately **$3 billion** in private U.S. hurricane donations, **$1.8 billion** for Indian Ocean tsunami relief, and **$128 million** for the Pakistan earthquake. Interviewees questioned whether what appeared as giving fatigue was instead households reaching their financial limits.
entries.assess: **As-of-date donations and respondents' opinions, not audited final receipts or disbursements.** Different disasters' fundraising windows and organizational definitions affect comparison; giving volumes do not alone measure whether aid reached intended beneficiaries.

entries.title: Sago families receive a false announcement of survival
entries.report: A student reporter revisited the January 2 Sago mine disaster in West Virginia: relatives briefly celebrated inaccurate news that twelve trapped miners had survived, before learning that only one was alive. The article emphasizes the anguish caused by communication failures.
entries.assess: **The false initial rescue news is part of the event's documented public history, not evidence that the eventual toll was concealed.** The Mine Safety and Health Administration's investigation documents **twelve deaths and one survivor**; some physical measurements and timings in the student's retelling are less reliable than the official investigation.

entries.title: Civil-rights organizing challenges Katrina recovery inequities
entries.report: Mathis's column describes a Rainbow/PUSH effort to press the federal government for more equitable help to displaced New Orleans residents, arguing that charitable donations alone could not redress barriers to return and rebuilding.
entries.assess: **Advocacy and interpretation**, not an independent audit establishing every asserted government failure. GAO contemporaneously documented significant post-hurricane social-service and education challenges; evaluating each proposed remedy requires subsequent implementation records.

entries.title: Children's Defense Fund warns of Katrina's long aftermath
entries.report: A report on the Children's Defense Fund's *Katrina's Children* called for mental-health treatment, mobile health facilities, school-based clinics, and easier Medicaid access for displaced and traumatized children.
entries.assess: **A documented advocacy program and unmet-needs warning, not proof every measure was enacted.** Subsequent GAO examinations show why schooling and child welfare posed substantial logistical problems, but intervention outcomes require separate data.

entries.title: New Orleans schools rebuild under contested charter arrangements
entries.report: Resseger criticized the post-Katrina reorganization of public schools and uncertainty created by school-by-school sponsorship, warning that the replacement of a centralized school system risked leaving vulnerable children without stable support.
entries.assess: **A contemporaneous policy critique**, not a neutral measure of charter-school performance. Subsequent aid and enrollment figures need comparison with the article's specific predictions before drawing a causal conclusion.

entries.title: Black-press editorial denounces destruction in Lebanon
entries.report: An editorial condemned civilian deaths and damage during the Israel–Hezbollah fighting and called for urgent international action to end attacks. It blamed multiple actors but clearly advocated a political position.
entries.assess: **Editorial assessment, not a final civilian-casualty investigation.** The Security Council adopted Resolution 1701 on **August 11**, calling for cessation of hostilities and an expanded UN role; the newspaper's publication followed the resolution and cannot stand as a full cease-fire compliance assessment.

entries.title: Column cites testimony alleging racial vigilantism after Katrina
entries.report: A religious-social-justice column quotes survivors' accounts gathered by a Katrina justice commission, alleging that armed vigilantes fired at or targeted African American men in the immediate aftermath of the storm.
entries.assess: **Serious attributed testimony, not a conviction record or independently established count of assaults.** The underlying witness interviews, police investigations, and any prosecutions must be checked individually; the fact that the claims were printed does not establish each alleged shooting or perpetrator.

leadingCandidate.evidence: title; curated candidate; headline and report reviewed

entries.title: Student column misidentifies North Korea's underground nuclear test
entries.report: A columnist called for stronger action against Kim Jong-il after the October North Korean test, but described an underground experiment as the detonation of a **'nuclear missile'**, conflating a nuclear-explosive test with a missile launch.
entries.assess: **The terminology in the student commentary is wrong.** The DPRK announced an underground nuclear-weapon test on **October 9, 2006**; the UN condemned that announced test and separately addressed ballistic-missile activity. Its exact yield cannot be inferred from the student's discussion of radiation reports.

entries.title: Katrina survivors' continuing housing hardship becomes a civil-rights argument
entries.report: Mathis argued that federal housing and rebuilding delays continued to injure displaced Gulf Coast families long after the storm and urged attention to people still struggling to return.
entries.assess: **Attributed political commentary**, not a household-level audit. The account is important evidence of dissatisfaction expressed in the Black press; exact assistance failures require administrative and survivor-specific records.

entries.title: William Jefferson indicted as his district continues hurricane recovery
entries.report: The column describes the then-recent **sixteen-count federal indictment** of Louisiana Congressman William Jefferson and argues that his district should not be deprived of Katrina recovery assistance because of its representative's legal troubles.
entries.assess: **At publication, the charged conduct was alleged rather than adjudicated.** A federal jury convicted Jefferson on **eleven counts in 2009**. Legal outcomes after that verdict need individual checking; the July 2007 indictment cannot be represented as a contemporaneous conviction.

entries.title: NAACP alleges racially discriminatory subprime lending
entries.report: The paper says the NAACP sued **fourteen lenders**, alleging African American borrowers faced disproportionately costly subprime loans, including some allegedly qualified for lower-cost products.
entries.assess: **A filed lawsuit and statistical allegations, not a verdict against all fourteen defendants.** Later federal investigations and settlements documented discriminatory-pricing and steering allegations involving particular lenders, but these cannot be retroactively treated as judgments on every defendant in the 2007 suit.
entries.proposedLeaf: Racially discriminatory lending, housing and economic exclusion
reviewFlags: proposed missing tertiary label; not adopted

leadingCandidate.evidence: curated candidate only; headline and report reviewed

entries.title: Nappanee eyewitnesses describe a violent nighttime tornado
entries.report: Residents recount the late-night **October 18** tornado and sudden damage to homes and a church. The paper prints a police department account of only moments to sound sirens and calls the tornado an 'F3.'
entries.assess: **Eyewitness testimony and immediate damage reporting.** Modern NWS documentation rates the tornado **EF3**, with estimated winds near **165 mph** over southeastern Nappanee; the original's older 'F3' wording should not be substituted for the Enhanced Fujita classification.

entries.title: Grade-school penny contest raises $3,750.49 for tornado victims
entries.report: Woodview Elementary students turned a grade-versus-grade penny contest into local tornado relief, with the paper reporting **$3,750.49 raised** and recalling their earlier fundraising after Katrina.
entries.assess: **Reported receipts for a specific school drive, not proof of how each dollar was subsequently distributed.** The beneficiary was the Nappanee Tornado Victims' Fund; expenditure records remain a separate research question.

entries.title: Long-term Nappanee tornado assistance remains available
entries.report: A local notice describes the Tornado Victims Assistance Fund, bank and card donation routes, and continued recovery services weeks after the October destruction.
entries.assess: **An advertised relief program, not a verified accounting of approvals, awards, or final recovery.** The repeated coverage shows that the local aftermath outlasted the initial national storm headlines.
entries.proposedLeaf: Long-term community recovery and reconstruction
reviewFlags: proposed missing tertiary label; not adopted

entries.title: Central Indiana mortgage-and-investment fraud conviction
entries.report: The paper reports that Indianapolis resident **Jason Keigley** was found guilty in Hendricks County Superior Court of crimes involving an investment and mortgage fraud scheme affecting older residents, citing state and county prosecutors.
entries.assess: **A reported court verdict, distinct from the much broader national mortgage crisis.** The original judgment, sentencing, appellate status, victim count, and restitution records have not yet been independently obtained.

leadingCandidate.evidence: curated candidate only; headline and report reviewed

entries.title: Bailout debate contrasts Wall Street rescue with foreclosures
entries.report: Mathis criticized the newly enacted **$700-billion financial rescue authorization** as insufficient relief for homeowners, while describing actions by state attorneys general against Countrywide mortgage practices.
entries.assess: **Policy argument with contemporary lawsuit and settlement reporting.** The $700 billion was a **program authorization**, not a verified lump-sum expenditure or a payment solely to a single institution. The column's broad assessment of homeowner relief must be separated from later program disbursements.

entries.title: Black Enterprise frames crash as a retirement-security threat
entries.report: A *Black Enterprise* retirement-planning feature linked falling retirement portfolios, collapsing financial firms including Lehman Brothers, and the housing bust to a crisis in long-term financial security.
entries.assess: **Contemporary consumer-finance framing, not a representative survey of retirement losses.** The Federal Reserve's later history distinguishes Lehman's failure from the support provided to some other firms; the economic categories must not be collapsed into 'all banks were bailed out.'

entries.title: Black press republishes Obama's historic victory speech
entries.report: The newspaper reproduced part of President-elect **Barack Obama's November 4 victory address**, coupling a landmark electoral outcome with his warning that war, financial crisis, and climate danger remained unresolved.
entries.assess: **A primary transcript of campaign rhetoric, not evidence that its policy promises were accomplished.** This page begins mid-speech; the complete address and certified election returns are better sources for exact wording and vote totals.

entries.title: Zimbabwe cholera toll in the press still climbing
entries.report: A feature on Zimbabwe's political and economic collapse says about **18,000 people** had contracted cholera and more than **1,111** had died according to reports circulating by publication.
entries.assess: **Mid-outbreak figures, not final totals.** WHO later reported **98,424 suspected cases and 4,276 deaths by May 30, 2009**. The article's unemployment and political characterizations should be attributed to its author rather than presented as independently audited statistics.

entries.title: Administration explains the frozen-credit cycle
entries.report: A continued address explains how mortgage losses, banks' fear of lending, and household and business credit constraints compounded unemployment and recession, while describing proposals to stabilize lending.
entries.assess: **An administration explanation of policy, not neutral proof of the planned rescue's results.** The excerpt starts on an earlier page; economic outcomes and costs must be checked against subsequent official data.

entries.title: H1N1 dispatch reports 403 U.S. cases and one death
entries.report: A dispatch describes international spread of the new swine-origin influenza A(H1N1) and quotes an early CDC tally of **403 U.S. cases and one death**, while expecting more cases and hospitalizations.
entries.assess: **An early surveillance snapshot, not the eventual epidemic total.** CDC later estimated approximately **60.8 million U.S. illnesses, 274,304 hospitalizations and 12,469 deaths** for April 2009–April 2010, with ranges reflecting statistical uncertainty.

entries.title: Lafayette school takes precautions during H1N1 wave
entries.report: Students described classroom sanitizers, hand-washing notices, absences and concerns about the emerging H1N1 vaccine; a second article expected first vaccine supplies during October.
entries.assess: **Direct local coverage of school response.** Vaccine distribution timing was prospective when written, and H1N1 was a real pandemic; neither panic nor a claim that all students were infected follows from precautions alone.

entries.title: Nappanee student absences and vaccinations provide a local flu snapshot
entries.report: A local reporting intern said one school week saw approximately **18 percent student absence** and around **300 immunizations**, while debunking common misconceptions about contracting H1N1 from pork.
entries.assess: **School-specific contemporaneous figures**, not a districtwide infection prevalence study. Absence does not prove laboratory-confirmed infection, and vaccine doses administered in this account do not establish population coverage.

entries.title: Black men's unemployment diverges sharply from national recession headline
entries.report: A news brief reports **more than 17 percent seasonally adjusted unemployment among Black men** in an October survey, versus lower rates for white men and women, drawing attention to unequal labor-market effects.
entries.assess: **A report of subgroup survey estimates, not 'one in five' for every Black adult or a direct census.** Definition, reference month, seasonal adjustment, and age category must be held constant before comparing BLS figures.
entries.proposedLeaf: Employment disparities and structural economic inequality
reviewFlags: proposed missing tertiary label; not adopted

entries.title: Haiti-earthquake story prints the wrong calendar year
entries.report: The student paper reports Haiti's devastating **magnitude-7.0** earthquake, relief needs, aftershocks and an interim estimate of **200,000 deaths**. In its main paragraph it accidentally dates the event **January 12, 2009**, even though the publication was in February 2010.
entries.assess: **A verifiable newspaper date error.** USGS records the earthquake on **January 12, 2010**. The paper's 200,000 figure was an interim, attributed estimate rather than an individually verified death register.

entries.title: Calls to cancel Haiti's foreign debt follow the quake
entries.report: A dispatch describes Representative Maxine Waters pressing the World Bank and other lenders for debt relief to help Haiti address urgent reconstruction costs.
entries.assess: **A documented appeal and legislative position, not evidence that every debt was forgiven immediately.** Outcomes would require examining the individual institutions' debt-relief decisions and disbursements.

entries.title: Black-press coverage asks whom health reform will reach
entries.report: The paper reported passage and signing of President Obama's health-care legislation, then examined its promises for Black patients and uninsured Americans. It referred to the **219–212** House vote.
entries.assess: **Passage and advocacy are distinct from measured coverage effects.** The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act was signed **March 23, 2010**; later enrollment, Medicaid expansion, and implementation need separate data.

entries.title: Gulf oil-spill columnist uses a then-current flow estimate
entries.report: Morial warned of prolonged Gulf Coast environmental and economic damage while saying the well had yet to be capped and repeating an early estimate of **over 200,000 gallons per day**.
entries.assess: **Contemporaneous concern and provisional flow-rate reporting, not a final release calculation.** NOAA subsequently assessed approximately **134 million gallons over 87 days** after the April 20 disaster that killed **eleven workers**.

entries.title: Nigerian oil-pollution inquiry draws dispute over evidence and funding
entries.report: Environmental groups criticized leaked characterizations of a UN environment study in the Niger Delta, questioned its dependence on oil-industry and government data, and raised concerns over Shell-related funding.
entries.assess: **Claims about a leaked draft and competing parties, not a verified finding that the final UN report blamed poor residents for the pollution.** UNEP published its substantive Ogoniland assessment in **2011**, documenting serious contamination and restoration needs; its actual text is the proper comparison.

entries.title: Tucson shooting prompts a high-school discussion of political rhetoric
entries.report: The school paper considers the January shooting of Representative Gabrielle Giffords and others in Tucson, and asks how political language and public safety should be discussed after mass violence.
entries.assess: **An editorial response, not a criminal investigation into the shooter's motive.** The causal influence of individual political statements cannot be established from commentary alone.

leadingCandidate.evidence: curated candidate only; headline and report reviewed

entries.title: Bin Laden's killing dominates the Black press front page
entries.report: The newspaper covered President Obama's announcement that U.S. forces killed al-Qaeda leader **Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad, Pakistan**, almost a decade after the September 11 attacks, and reported public reactions.
entries.assess: **The death and operation were officially announced; some immediate operational details remained subject to revision and later disclosure.** The front page is contemporaneous public reaction, not a complete special-operations record.

entries.title: Newspaper prints the president's description of the operation
entries.report: The paper reproduced the president's speech framing bin Laden's death in relation to the victims of September 11 and the longer campaign against al-Qaeda.
entries.assess: **An official account reproduced by a newspaper, not an independent verification of each operational step.** Presidential claims, intelligence timelines, and subsequent military reporting have different evidentiary roles.

entries.title: Occupy protest movement interpreted from a high-school editorial page
entries.report: A student editorial portrays Occupy protests as a response to the prolonged recession, inequality, rising education costs, and the influence of wealth in politics, while considering the drawbacks of intentionally leaderless organizing.
entries.assess: **A published interpretation of protesters' concerns, not a formal national platform or demographic study.** The editorial compares Occupy to the Tea Party as a political analogy, not as proof that the two movements had equivalent policies.

entries.title: Brownsville school shooting turns on whether a weapon was real
entries.report: A reporter describes police shooting **eighth-grader Jaime González** at Cummings Middle School in Brownsville, Texas, on **January 4**, after responding to a report that he had a gun; the weapon was subsequently described as a pellet gun.
entries.assess: **The student article is a secondary account of a fatal police encounter.** It does not establish exactly what responding officers could see or whether their actions were lawful; dispatch audio, investigative findings, and court records remain unreviewed here.

entries.title: Pre-election analysis treats swing states as unresolved
entries.report: Editor-in-chief Kate Halliwell assessed the Obama–Romney contest just before voting, treating undecided voters and competitive states as capable of altering the result.
entries.assess: **A forecast written before the count, not certified returns.** Its uncertainty belongs to **November 2**, even though the result became clear days later.

entries.title: Student press debates the Electoral College after Obama's reelection
entries.report: Two school columnists debate whether the Electoral College adequately represents voters after the presidential election, contrasting institutional stability against critiques of unequal representation.
entries.assess: **A paired editorial debate, not a legal change or proven finding of election fraud.** The disagreement shows how younger readers were interpreting election rules immediately afterward.

entries.title: Hurricane Sandy's perceived electoral impact is debated
entries.report: A post-election school article notes Obama's victory and reports speculation that **Hurricane Sandy** influenced public perceptions during the campaign's final days.
entries.assess: **A proposed electoral explanation, not a causal finding.** NOAA documents Sandy's destructive physical impacts and **147 direct fatalities** in the storm's broader affected region; storm consequences and voter behavior must not be conflated.

entries.title: Paulsboro bridge derailment releases hazardous vinyl chloride
entries.report: A story describes a **November 30** freight-train derailment on a New Jersey movable bridge, cars entering Mantua Creek, and the danger posed by vinyl chloride in the damaged cars.
entries.assess: **The event and hazardous release are corroborated.** The NTSB ultimately traced the derailment to proceeding past a red signal with bridge-locks not fully engaged and inadequate crew training; the student account's broad environmental fears are not a substitute for exposure measurements.

reviewFlags: proposed missing tertiary label; not adopted

entries.title: Student report accurately counts Sandy Hook's 26 school victims
entries.report: A high-school writer describes the **December 14, 2012** shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary in Newtown, Connecticut, identifying **twenty children and six adult staff** as the school victims and noting the killing of the attacker's mother separately.
entries.assess: **The school victim count is corroborated** but exact terminology about the attack and the perpetrator still requires precision. The 26 were killed at the school; the perpetrator's mother was a separate victim elsewhere.

entries.title: School-security follow-up misdates Sandy Hook by three days
entries.report: An article describes safety notices sent to parents and debate over school security after the Newtown massacre, but places the attack on **December 17**, rather than December 14, 2012.
entries.assess: **A demonstrable date error within real aftermath reporting.** The massacre occurred **December 14**. This kind of misdating is evidence of imperfect editing/OCR and reporting, not of a second school attack on December 17.
entries.proposedLeaf: School safety and institutional responses
reviewFlags: proposed missing tertiary label; not adopted

entries.title: Boston bombing chronology reconstructed for students
entries.report: A student writer reconstructs the **April 15 Boston Marathon bombing**, subsequent release of suspect photographs, and the confusing days of carjacking, the death of an MIT officer and the manhunt.
entries.assess: **Retrospective journalism within weeks of the event, not a complete trial record.** DOJ's June indictment identifies the allegations against Dzhokhar Tsarnaev; charges and early press identification must be kept separate from later judicial findings.

entries.title: Student column describes the costs of the federal shutdown
entries.report: A student columnist criticizes the partisan impasse that idled many federal operations and workers during the October government shutdown and worries about future deadlines.
entries.assess: **Editorial attribution of political blame is not an official causal finding.** GAO documented a **sixteen-day partial shutdown** from the lapse in appropriations; effects varied by agency, employee category, and specific appropriations authority.

entries.title: Indiana charity appeals for Typhoon Haiyan survivors
entries.report: A short item solicited funds and essential supplies for survivors of the **November 8** Philippine super-typhoon, describing displacement, destroyed homes, and urgent demands for water, food and shelter.
entries.assess: **An appeal is proof of fundraising outreach, not shipment or final distribution.** The UN later recorded **over 6,300 deaths**; the paper's early needs figures and imperfect digitized text should not be used as the final humanitarian ledger.

entries.title: Student newspaper tracks Ukraine's upheaval and Crimea dispute
entries.report: A student feature links protests against President Viktor Yanukovych, his decision against an EU association agreement, and Russia's move into Crimea; its presentation reflects fast-changing reports and contested political narratives.
entries.assess: **An early explanation, not a neutral referendum audit.** UN General Assembly Resolution **68/262** subsequently affirmed Ukraine's territorial integrity and called on states not to recognize a change to Crimea's status based on the March vote.

entries.title: Commentary treats Putin's move into Crimea as a turning point
entries.report: A columnist discusses Russian forces entering Crimea and the protests in Kyiv, focusing on the risk of escalation and the extent of President Vladimir Putin's ambitions.
entries.assess: **Contemporary interpretation, not privileged evidence of Putin's internal decision-making.** The later purported annexation is widely rejected under Ukraine's territorial integrity; the article's speculative predictions must remain forecasts.

entries.title: Ferguson reporting explicitly repeats a rumored quotation
entries.report: An opinion article about protests after **Michael Brown's August 9 death** opens with the widely circulated 'Hands up, don't shoot' account but labels it **rumored** and notes conflicting eyewitness statements.
entries.assess: **Do not convert the disputed slogan into a verified last quotation.** The later DOJ investigation concluded the evidence did not support federal charges against officer Darren Wilson and found key surrender accounts inconsistent with credible evidence. That finding is distinct from DOJ's separate finding of systemic unconstitutional policing practices in Ferguson.

entries.title: Ebola article captures genuine health anxiety and loose epidemic language
entries.report: A student report describes widespread fear of the West African Ebola outbreak and reports thousands of infections, using alarming terminology and loosely combining affected African countries.
entries.assess: **Fear and early case counts are historical evidence of perception, not evidence that Ebola spreads like airborne seasonal flu or was epidemic across the United States.** CDC records a large West African epidemic but **eleven patients treated in the U.S. and two deaths** during that outbreak.

entries.title: Editorial follows Thomas Eric Duncan's U.S. Ebola case
entries.report: The paper discusses **Thomas Eric Duncan**, who arrived from Liberia, was initially discharged from a Texas hospital, received an Ebola diagnosis, and died on **October 8**, while considering medical response and public fear.
entries.assess: **The central clinical chronology is supported by CDC**, but allegations of widespread domestic transmission are unwarranted. CDC identifies two nurses infected while caring for a patient in the U.S.; separate imported cases do not imply uncontrolled national community spread.

entries.title: Student opinion tracks the rise and threats of ISIS
entries.report: The column describes Islamic State's territorial expansion in Iraq and Syria, threats against civilians, and violent propaganda, with several large territorial and population figures attributed to other media.
entries.assess: **A topical opinion account, not a verified population census or independent order-of-battle assessment.** Geographic control and the number of people under ISIS rule changed quickly; quantitative claims must be dated and separately sourced.

entries.title: Ferguson grand-jury decision renews protest and disputed legal descriptions
entries.report: The article describes renewed protests after a grand jury declined to indict officer Darren Wilson, mixing accounts of peaceful demonstrations and property damage. It uses 'trial' loosely in discussing the grand jury.
entries.assess: **A grand-jury nonindictment is not an acquittal after a jury trial.** DOJ's March 2015 findings separately declined federal criminal charges in Brown's shooting while documenting a pattern of unconstitutional policing and municipal-court practices. Both outcomes must be retained.

entries.title: Student reporter details the Charlie Hebdo massacre and free-expression debate
entries.report: A feature reports the **January 7** attack on the French satirical weekly *Charlie Hebdo*, names the Kouachi brothers, and considers how violent extremism and offense taken at cartoons intersected with freedom of expression.
entries.assess: **Real attack, but explanatory discussions of the attackers' beliefs are not proof that an entire religion endorsed violence.** The newsroom assault killed **twelve**; related January Paris attacks bring the wider sequence's total to **seventeen**, a different casualty definition.
entries.proposedLeaf: Ideologically motivated shootings and coordinated terrorist attacks
reviewFlags: proposed missing tertiary label; not adopted

entries.title: Indiana students take opposing positions on religious-freedom law
entries.report: The school paper debates Indiana's recently enacted Religious Freedom Restoration Act amid concern over LGBT discrimination, private-business practices, boycotts and conscience protections.
entries.assess: **Competing legal and ethical arguments, not court holdings.** Indiana enacted **SEA 101 in March**, then adopted **SEA 50's clarifications in April**; characterizations of what businesses could lawfully do must account for the amendment and other applicable laws.

entries.title: School-gun debate cites Oregon and Sandy Hook after new shooting
entries.report: A student discussion of gun policy invokes the **October 1 Umpqua Community College** attack and the earlier Sandy Hook massacre to argue over gun availability, school safety and the Second Amendment.
entries.assess: **A policy argument built around genuine events, not a controlled study proving the effect of any proposed gun law.** The causal and constitutional claims are the students' positions; outcomes depend on legislation and evidence not examined in this record.

entries.title: Syrian refugee crisis enters a student foreign-policy debate
entries.report: A student article tracks the Syrian civil war, neighboring countries taking refugees, and the difficult choices facing the United States and Europe while ISIS terrorism dominated debate.
